Package: Workstream W1-docs-site, Delorun's documentation website. One package: WP1.8, Documentation website, Delorun's own Fumadocs site (Model cell: Haiku, high).
Repository and branch: Delo-Run/delo, in a worktree of your own on branch `wave1/docs-site`, base `v5`.
Read first: The root `AGENTS.md`; `docs/AGENTS.md`, its section on Delorun's documentation website and its bilingual and word-budget rules; `docs/i18n/README.md` for the English and Chinese pairs; the documentation tier index `delorun/docs/README.md` with `delorun/docs/guide/README.md` and `delorun/docs/reference/README.md`; the tools README `delorun/apps/tools/README.md`, its local checks section; the workflow skill `.agents/skills/delorun-dev-workflow/SKILL.md`; the delegation skill `.agents/skills/delorun-delegation/SKILL.md`, its workstreams and standard rulings; `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, whose `!delorun/apps/docs` line keeps the site out of the root workspace; the changelog rules `delorun/changelog/unreleased/README.md`.
Goal: Build Delorun's documentation website as a Fumadocs site with its own lockfile and a dead-link check, publishing every page under `delorun/docs/guide/` and `delorun/docs/reference/` in English and Chinese, with a `docs-site` lane in Delorun's check runner.
You own: `delorun/apps/docs/` (new: the site, its package manifest, its own pnpm lockfile, its README pair and its ignore file); the `docs-site` lane in `delorun/apps/tools/src/checks/plan.ts` and `delorun/apps/tools/src/checks/budgets.json`, with its selection specs in `delorun/apps/tools/tests/checks.spec.ts`; the check table and the site's line in `delorun/apps/tools/README.md`, `delorun/apps/tools/README.zh.md` and `delorun/apps/tools/README.i18n.yaml`; the website paragraph of `docs/AGENTS.md`, which says the tree does not contain the site's README. Change nothing else; if you must, stop and report.
Interfaces: The check entry type and the `catalog` function in `delorun/apps/tools/src/checks/plan.ts`, and the budget file `delorun/apps/tools/src/checks/budgets.json`, used exactly as written. The page sources are the pairs under `delorun/docs/guide/` and `delorun/docs/reference/`: each page `<name>.md` has its Chinese page `<name>.zh.md` beside it, and the `*.i18n.yaml` files are pairing records, not pages.
Pattern to follow: `website/docs.ts`, upstream's publication manifest, for mapping each source pair into the two locale route trees without copying Markdown; the `parity-replay` entry in `delorun/apps/tools/src/checks/plan.ts` for a lane that runs only when its paths change.
Steps:
1. Set up the worktree with `node delorun/apps/tools/src/setup-worktree.ts` on the Node major that `.nvmrc` pins.
2. Create the site in the owned directory as a private package (`"private": true`, licence MIT) with its own pnpm lockfile beside its manifest; it is outside the root workspace, so install it with `(cd delorun/apps && pnpm --dir docs install)`.
3. Read the page pairs from `delorun/docs/guide/` and `delorun/docs/reference/` in place, never copied: English at the site root, Chinese under the `zh/` route prefix. Each page names the Delorun version it describes, from one source the site's README names.
4. Serve each page also as Markdown, with `llms.txt` indexes.
5. For harness topics, link upstream's published documentation; never copy a page from `docs/` or `website/`.
6. Make the build fail on a dead internal link or anchor, in both locales. External links are not fetched.
7. Add the `docs-site` check to the catalogue with its budget: it runs the site's build, it is selected when a path under the site's directory or `delorun/docs/` changes, and it fails with a message naming the install command when the site's dependencies are missing. Add the selection specs.
8. Write the site's README pair: its routes, the install and build commands, the dead-link check, and how deployment works. Update the tools README pair and the `docs/AGENTS.md` paragraph, and re-record each pairing file with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <path>`.
9. Escalate, then wait, when: a change would move an approval, a refusal or an escalation; a contract would change; the work needs an owner decision, such as a deploy, a hosting account, the `docs.delorun.com` domain or another publication; a test cannot pass honestly; or a file outside the owned paths must change, such as `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or a gate. List every other decision in the report.
10. Merge order: this workstream has one package and one pull request. Rebase onto `v5`, push the branch through Delorun's pre-push gate, open the pull request, and fast-forward `v5` once the gate passes and the review approves. Another Wave 1 workstream also edits the tools README pair; after a rebase keep both changes and re-record the pairing file.
Acceptance:
`(cd delorun/apps && pnpm --dir docs install --frozen-lockfile)` exits 0.
The site's build command named in its README, such as `(cd delorun/apps && pnpm --dir docs run build)`, exits 0 and runs the dead-link check; a planted dead link makes it exit non-zero.
The built site holds a page in English and one in Chinese for every page under `delorun/docs/guide/` and `delorun/docs/reference/`, each also served as Markdown, and the `llms.txt` indexes.
`git diff --exit-code v5 -- website/` exits 0: upstream's VitePress tree is unmodified.
`node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config delorun/vitest.config.ts delorun/apps/tools/tests/checks.spec.ts` passes, with cases showing that a change under the site's directory or `delorun/docs/` selects `docs-site` and that another change does not.
`pnpm check -- --plan` lists `docs-site` for this branch, and `pnpm check` exits 0.
Security notes: No trust boundary moves. The site is static: no analytics, remote fonts or third-party scripts, and the build makes no network request after the install; disable the framework's telemetry in the build script (for Next.js, `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`). Every new dependency is pinned in the site's lockfile and carries a licence the licence gate accepts. The site publishes only `delorun/docs/` pages and upstream links: no secret, personal data or infrastructure identifier reaches a page.
Documentation: Package tier: the site's README pair in the owned directory, with its pairing record. Delorun tooling tier: the check table in `delorun/apps/tools/README.md` with `delorun/apps/tools/README.zh.md`. Documentation rules: the website paragraph in `docs/AGENTS.md`. No changelog fragment: the site is not published by this package, so end each commit that touches the site with `Changelog: none (documentation site build, not published)`.
Report: Files changed, every command run with its result, each decision taken under the standard rulings, open questions, and any contract or interface change you propose.
Never: Push to `v5` other than the fast-forward the merge order describes, merge another branch, deploy or publish the site, contact a live provider, add secrets, modify `website/`, or skip a hook.

Package: Workstream W1-rehearse, the upstream rehearsal merge. One package: WP1.14, Upstream rehearsal merge and divergence budget (Model cell: Opus, high; lead review).
Size and review: M; standard review, and the lead reviews the result before `v5` moves
Repository and branch: Delo-Run/delo, in a worktree of your own on branch `wave1/rehearse-upstream`, base `v5`.
Read first: The root `AGENTS.md`, its fork boundary section; the divergence index `delorun/docs/reference/divergence/README.md`, its classes and its divergence budget; the ledger `delorun/upstream-patches.json` and its schema `delorun/upstream-patches.schema.json`; the tools README `delorun/apps/tools/README.md`, its divergence ledger and local checks sections; the workflow skill `.agents/skills/delorun-dev-workflow/SKILL.md`; the delegation skill `.agents/skills/delorun-delegation/SKILL.md`, its workstreams and standard rulings.
Goal: Add `rehearse-upstream.ts`, which merges a given upstream tag into a scratch worktree, prints the conflicted paths and the ledger's growth per class against the divergence budget, and exits 1 when the merge breaks the budget.
You own: `delorun/apps/tools/src/rehearse-upstream.ts` (new); `delorun/apps/tools/tests/rehearse/` (new, with its fixture builders); the modules list and a new rehearsal section in `delorun/apps/tools/README.md`, `delorun/apps/tools/README.zh.md` and `delorun/apps/tools/README.i18n.yaml`; the rehearsal merge bullet in `delorun/docs/reference/divergence/README.md`, `delorun/docs/reference/divergence/README.zh.md` and `delorun/docs/reference/divergence/README.i18n.yaml`. Change nothing else; if you must, stop and report.
Contracts consumed: None. The divergence budget in `delorun/docs/reference/divergence/README.md` is the rule set, used exactly as written.
Interfaces: From `delorun/apps/tools/src/check-fork-boundary.ts`: `readManifest`, `changedSince`, `hunkCount`, `measureDivergence` and `formatDivergence`. From `delorun/apps/tools/src/fork-boundary.ts`: `MANIFEST_PATH`, `parseManifest`, `PatchManifest`, `Patch`, `RetiredEntry`, `Divergence` and `divergence`. From `delorun/apps/tools/src/git.ts`: `runGit`, `git` and `repositoryRoot`. All used exactly as written; compute anything they lack, such as the count per class, inside the new module.
Pattern to follow: `delorun/apps/tools/src/check-fork-boundary.ts` for a command line over the ledger that prints the divergence; `delorun/apps/tools/tests/ledger-merge.integration.spec.ts` for specs that build temporary git repositories and merge in them.
Steps:
1. Set up the worktree with `node delorun/apps/tools/src/setup-worktree.ts` on the Node major that `.nvmrc` pins.
2. Parse `--tag <tag>` (required) and resolve the request into one explicit spec: the tag, the upstream repository from the ledger's `upstream.repository`, and the current pin.
3. Fetch the tag, create a scratch worktree in a temporary directory, detached at the current `HEAD`, and merge the tag's commit there without committing. Remove the scratch worktree whatever the outcome, and leave the person's checkout, branches and index unchanged.
4. Print the conflicted paths, and the conflicted hunks as a share of the ledger's hunks at the tag.
5. Measure the ledger at the tag against the current count, per class (`delorun-feature`, `generic-fix`, `security`), in entries and hunks, crediting each entry the tag absorbs. Print the growth beside each cap. Until the first release's baseline is recorded, the caps are the floors the budget names: 20 entries and 150 hunks.
6. Exit 1, with one line per failure, when growth exceeds a cap, when conflicted hunks exceed 15 % of the ledger's hunks at the tag, or when a `security`-class file conflicts without a recorded maintainer decision. The ledger has no field for that decision, so every `security`-class conflict fails; propose where the decision is recorded in the report. The ledger also marks no entry as generated, so count every entry, print that generated entries are not separated, and raise it in the report.
7. Write specs with fixture repositories built in temporary directories: a merge within budget exits 0; each of the three failures exits 1 with its line; an absorbed entry is credited; the scratch worktree is gone after a failed run. No spec reaches the network.
8. Document the command in the tools README pair and the divergence page pair, and re-record each pairing file with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <path>`.
9. Escalate, then wait, when: a change would move an approval, a refusal or an escalation; a contract would change, including the ledger's schema; the budget needs a decision the divergence page leaves to a maintainer or the owner; a test cannot pass honestly; or a file outside the owned paths must change. List every other decision in the report.
10. Merge order: this workstream has one package and one pull request. Rebase onto `v5`, push the branch through Delorun's pre-push gate, open the pull request, and wait for the lead's review before `v5` is fast-forwarded. Another Wave 1 workstream also edits the tools README pair; after a rebase keep both changes and re-record the pairing file.
Acceptance:
`node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config delorun/vitest.config.ts rehearse` passes, running the new specs, with one case for each of the three failures, one within budget and one for an absorbed entry.
The new command, run from the repository root with `node_modules/.bin/tsx` and without `--tag`, exits non-zero with a usage line.
After any run, `git worktree list` shows no scratch worktree and `git status --porcelain` is unchanged.
`node_modules/.bin/tsx delorun/apps/tools/src/check-fork-boundary.ts` exits 0, and `pnpm check` exits 0.
Record in the report, as a manual check, the output of a run against upstream's newest tag.
Security notes: The rehearsal reads only: it never commits, pushes, re-pins the ledger or changes the person's checkout, and it removes its scratch worktree on every path. The specs use local fixture repositories only, never a real remote. The `security`-class rule stays strict: without a recorded decision every such conflict fails.
Documentation: Delorun tooling tier: the modules list and the rehearsal section in `delorun/apps/tools/README.md` with `delorun/apps/tools/README.zh.md`. Reference tier: the rehearsal merge bullet in `delorun/docs/reference/divergence/README.md` with `delorun/docs/reference/divergence/README.zh.md`. JSDoc on every export of the new module. These paths need no changelog fragment; `Changelog: none (repository tooling)` is accepted.
Report: Files changed, every command run with its result, the manual run's output, each decision taken under the standard rulings, the proposed record for a maintainer's `security`-class decision and for generated entries, open questions, and any contract or interface change you propose.
Never: Push to `v5` other than the fast-forward the merge order describes, merge another branch, merge an upstream tag into a real branch, change `delorun/upstream-patches.json`, deploy, contact a live provider, add secrets, or skip a hook.
